50	`agent.md` is the project's guide for agents — package names, key files, run command. Keep it terse and concrete: bullet points, no prose essays.
51	
52	The run command lives here (and in `Taskfile.yml` when the blueprint ships one). It's a plain `dapr run` invocation; what's load-bearing in it:
53	
54	- **`--app-id`** must match `Constants.ComponentName` (which is also what gets passed to `AddIntropyFramework(x => x.ComponentName = ...)`). It's the identity Dapr uses for the sidecar.
55	- **`--resources-path`** points at the directory of Dapr component YAMLs (`./local/dapr-components`). Keep it in sync with the actual on-disk path.
56	- **`--app-port`** (when the component has web endpoints) must match the `--urls` port in the `dotnet run` part of the command. If you change one, change the other.
57	
58	If you add a new Dapr component, you generally **don't** need to touch the run command — the sidecar discovers everything in the resources path. The component YAMLs themselves are covered by `intropy-dapr`.
59	
60	Update `agent.md` whenever the facts it states change, so the next agent invocation has accurate context:
61	
62	- Added a state store, a binding, or a second pub/sub under `local/dapr-components/`.
63	- Renamed a topic or component (bump `Constants.cs` and the Dapr YAML in the same change).
64	- Changed the run command or ports.
65	
66	## What to avoid
67	
68	- **Don't let `--app-id` and `Constants.ComponentName` drift.** The mismatch is silent at compile time and shows up as Dapr identity confusion at runtime. Change both in the same commit.
69	- **Don't point `--resources-path` at a path that doesn't exist** — the sidecar starts with no components and messages disappear into the void.
70	- **Don't let `agent.md` go stale.** A wrong run command or missing component listing misleads every future agent session in the repo. If the blueprint ships a `Taskfile.yml`, keep its vars in sync too.
71	
72	## Verification
73	
74	- The run command in `agent.md` starts the component under Dapr — run it from the component root and confirm the app comes up on its app port and the sidecar loads the components from `local/dapr-components/`.
75	- Confirm the run command's `--app-id` matches `Constants.ComponentName` in `src/Configuration/Constants.cs`.
76	- Skim `agent.md` and check that its run command, ports, and component listing match `Taskfile.yml` (if present) and `local/dapr-components/`.

2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code when working in this repository.
4	
5	## What this repo is
6	
7	A library of **Intropy blueprints**. Each blueprint is a scaffold-style template
8	rendered into a working project by the `intropy` CLI (separate repo:
9	`integrio-intropy/intropy-cli`). The CLI is the only renderer; this repo
10	contains content, not code.
11	
12	The model is intentionally narrow: one engine (Go `text/template` + sprig),
13	one manifest format, one source of truth per blueprint.
14	
15	## Repository layout
16	
17	```
18	<blueprint>/
19	  template.yaml          # required: the intropy.dev/v1 manifest
20	  skeleton/              # required: rendered into the user's --output
21	    <files…>             # `.tmpl` files are templated; everything else is copied
22	  README.md              # optional: author-facing — what this blueprint produces
23	  examples/              # optional: test fixtures for local renders
24	    minimal.yaml
25	    full.yaml
26	```
27	
28	Rules:
29	
30	- The CLI selects a blueprint via positional argument:
31	  `intropy int create hello-world -o ./out`.
32	- Only `<blueprint>/template.yaml` is parsed; only `<blueprint>/skeleton/` is
33	  walked by the renderer.
34	- Anything else at the blueprint root (README, examples, CHANGELOG, ADRs) is
35	  invisible to the renderer — it's for the blueprint author, not the
36	  scaffolded project.
37	- There is **no shared content between blueprints**. No repo-level
38	  `skeletons/` dir, no cross-blueprint includes. If two blueprints need the
39	  same file, duplicate it.
40	
41	## Manifest schema (`<blueprint>/template.yaml`)
42	
43	```yaml
44	apiVersion: intropy.dev/v1
45	kind: Template
46	metadata:
47	  name: <kebab-case>           # convention: match the directory name
48	  title: <Title Case>
49	  description: <one sentence>
50	  tags: [example, go, http]
51	  labels:                      # free-form; no key is load-bearing today
52	    intropy.io/template-level: example
53	spec:
54	  parameters:                  # raw JSON Schema; type must be "object"
55	    type: object
56	    required: [name]
57	    properties:
58	      name:
59	        type: string
60	        title: Service name
61	        description: Lowercase kebab-case identifier.
62	        pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
63	      port:
64	        type: integer
65	        default: 8080
66	  values:                      # optional; derived values rendered via Go template + sprig
67	    module: 'github.com/example/{{ .name }}'
68	```
69	
70	Notes:
71	
72	- **`spec.parameters` is plain JSON Schema.** Types: `string`, `boolean`,
73	  `integer`, `number`. Supported attributes: `title`, `description`, `pattern`,
74	  `enum`, `default`. The same schema validates CLI inputs and drives the
75	  Backstage form when a Template entity references this blueprint.
76	- **Parameter declaration order matters** for human display. Keep the YAML
77	  order intentional.
78	- **`spec.values` derives string values from parameters.** Each entry is a Go
79	  template (with sprig) rendered against the resolved parameters. Use for
80	  composite values needed in multiple skeleton files (e.g. a module path).
81	  Output is always a string. Don't chain entries — map iteration order
82	  is non-deterministic.
83	- **No `spec.steps`**, no `spec.owner`, no `nextSteps`. The model is
84	  intentionally narrow: a manifest declares parameters and the skeleton tree
85	  describes what gets written.
86	
87	## Skeleton conventions (`<blueprint>/skeleton/`)
88	
89	- **File contents are templated only if the filename ends in `.tmpl`.** The
90	  `.tmpl` suffix is stripped on output (`README.md.tmpl` → `README.md`).
91	- **Filenames and directory names are templated** with the same `{{ .param }}`
92	  syntax as file contents (e.g. `src/{{ .name }}.csproj`). The `.tmpl` suffix
93	  only governs whether *file contents* are rendered; path segments are always
94	  templated.
95	- **Use `{{ .paramName }}` to reference parameters and derived values.** The
96	  data context is a flat map containing parameters + `spec.values` entries.
97	- **Sprig is available.** `upper`, `lower`, `title`, `kebabcase`,
98	  `snakecase`, `replace`, `default`, `trim`, `len`, `get`, `dict`. Full list:
99	  https://masterminds.github.io/sprig/ .
100	- **Missing keys are a hard error.** The renderer runs with
101	  `missingkey=error`. Typos like `{{ .Name }}` (wrong case) fail the render
102	  with a clear message — they don't silently produce empty strings.
103	- **Sprig functions with side effects exist** (`env`, `now`, `uuidv4`,
104	  `getHostByName`). Don't use them — they break the "same inputs → same
105	  output" reproducibility guarantee.
106	
107	Example skeleton file `skeleton/README.md.tmpl`:
108	
109	```markdown
110	# {{ .name }}
111	
112	Generated from the `{{ .name }}` blueprint.
113	
114	Module: `{{ .module }}`
115	```
116

118	
119	1. Create the directory: `mkdir -p <name>/skeleton <name>/examples`.
120	2. Write `<name>/template.yaml` (manifest).
121	3. Write skeleton files under `<name>/skeleton/`. Suffix anything you want
122	   templated with `.tmpl`.
123	4. Write `<name>/README.md` describing what the blueprint produces and what

## The decision

**agent.md is the per-project manifest for agents** — the facts no skill can know: what the component is, its component/topic/binding names, ports, app id, key-file map, how to run it, and deliberate deviations (like transactional's omitted idempotency). **Skills own all generic teaching.** The run command has one canonical home: `task run` when the blueprint ships a Taskfile (transactional), otherwise the raw `dapr run` in agent.md (hello-world). Each agent.md ends with a single pointer to the skills collection — no per-skill routing table.

## What changed

**Blueprints repo** (`~/dev/intropy/blueprints`):
- `CLAUDE.md` — new "The agent.md convention" section documenting the contract for future blueprint authors.
- `hello-world/skeleton/agent.md.tmpl` — facts only; fixed the port from 5000 to **5001** (README and the `.http` file already used 5001, so the old command broke the sample requests); added the missing `local-storage` binding and `Endpoints.cs`/`Process/` to the facts; dropped the generic `.WithTopic`/naming-sync teaching.

- `transactional/skeleton/README.md.tmpl` — same fix: `task run` instead of the stale manual seed + raw command.

**Skills repo** (`~/dev/intropy/skills`):
- `intropy-manifest/SKILL.md` — codifies the sharpened contract: facts-only rule, Taskfile-canonical run command, skills-pointer convention, plus two new "what to avoid" bullets.
- `intropy-getting-started/SKILL.md` — transactional first-run now goes through `task run`; run-command guidance updated to match.

# Intropy Documentation

The shared foundation for writing any Intropy documentation in Backstage TechDocs.

This skill covers writing conventions, TechDocs structure, Intropy domain model
terminology, and templates for every type of documentation page in the Intropy
ecosystem. Whether you're writing a block reference page, a blueprint pattern spec,
an archetype overview, or a setup guide — start here.

## When NOT to use this skill

For per-blueprint golden path tutorials that walk developers through scaffolded
Backstage template code (explaining TODOs, file-by-file walkthroughs), use the
**blueprint-golden-path** skill instead. This skill covers the WHAT and WHY;
blueprint-golden-path covers the HOW step-by-step.

## What this skill covers

| Documentation type | Template | When to use |
|-------------------|----------|-------------|
| **Block reference page** | `references/block-template.md` | Documenting what a generic block type IS (Extractor, Loader, etc.) |
| **Blueprint pattern page** | `references/blueprint-template.md` | Documenting a named composition as a reusable pattern (Golden Record, etc.) |
| **Archetype page** | `references/archetype-template.md` | Documenting an abstract behavioural model (Pub/Sub, Aggregator, API Service) |
| **Connector concept page** | `references/connector-reference.md` | Explaining what Connectors are and how they relate to Blocks |

## Workflow

### 1. Understand what you're writing

Determine which type of documentation the user needs. If they say "document the
Extractor", that's a block reference page. If they say "write up the Golden Record
pattern", that's a blueprint pattern page. If they're unclear, ask.

For the **full pattern reference catalog** (all blocks + blueprints + archetypes),
use the scaffold script:

```bash
python scripts/scaffold.py --type catalog --output-dir ./output
```

### 2. Read the relevant references

**Always read first:**
- `references/intropy-model.md` — The authoritative domain model. Read this to use
  terminology correctly. Blocks, Blueprints, Connectors, Systems, Integrations,
  and Archetypes all have precise meanings.

**Then read the relevant template:**
- Block page → `references/block-template.md`
- Blueprint page → `references/blueprint-template.md`
- Archetype page → `references/archetype-template.md`
- Connector explanation → `references/connector-reference.md`
- Architecture overview → `references/architecture-overview-template.md`

**For TechDocs structure and MkDocs configuration:**
- `references/techdocs-structure.md` — File layout, mkdocs.yml patterns, catalog-info.yaml

### 3. Write using Intropy conventions

These principles apply to ALL Intropy documentation, regardless of type.

**Use terminology precisely.** The Intropy model has specific terms with specific
meanings. A Connector is not a "plugin" — it's accumulated organizational knowledge
about an external system. A Blueprint is not a "template" — it's a named composition
of Block types. Read `references/intropy-model.md` if unsure.

**Describe the invariant, not the variant.** When writing about generic patterns
(blocks, blueprints, archetypes), every sentence should be true for ALL instances.
"An Extractor pulls data from a source system" — not "An Extractor pulls data from
Dynamics." Specific systems belong in golden path tutorials, not reference pages.

**Define responsibility boundaries clearly.** The most important thing about a block
or blueprint doc is where responsibilities start and stop. An Extractor handles
source system communication but does NOT transform data into the internal model.
These boundaries are what make blocks composable.

**Explain the failure model.** Edge blocks handle business errors (expected operational
conditions). Core blocks treat bad input as bugs (unexpected). This distinction is
fundamental. Make it prominent and concrete with generic examples.

**Show the Connector contract.** For edge blocks, the Connector interface is what
makes them reusable across systems. Document the generic interface — what any
Connector must provide — so Connector developers know what to implement.

**Use TechDocs admonitions.** Use MkDocs admonition syntax for callouts:

```markdown
!!! info "Why does this matter?"
    Explanation of architectural reasoning.

!!! warning "Common mistake"
    What goes wrong and how to avoid it.

!!! note "Prerequisites"
    What the reader needs before continuing.
```

**Cross-reference generously.** Every block page should link to its archetype page
and the blueprints it appears in. Every blueprint page should link to its block
pages. Every archetype page should link to the blocks that follow it. This
bidirectional linking reinforces the conceptual framework.

### 4. Structure for TechDocs

Read `references/techdocs-structure.md` for the full details. The essentials:

- **techdocs-core** is the only allowed MkDocs plugin
- **nav is required** — TechDocs uses it for the sidebar
- Use `assets/mkdocs-template.yml` as the base configuration
- File naming: lowercase, hyphenated (e.g., `transactional-integration.md`)
- Every TechDocs site needs a `catalog-info.yaml` for Backstage registration
